```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
```

## Start with a map

`hcmap()` selects a map from the [Highcharts collection](https://code.highcharts.com/mapdata/)
and creates the map widget. The rest of the chart API works as usual. These
examples use local snapshots of those official boundaries, so the maps also
work without a CDN request. `hcmap()` accepts either a collection name or an
already loaded GeoJSON list. Keep the map attribution visible when publishing.

```{r map-directory}
map_dir <- here::here("dev", "examples-charts", "data", "maps")
```

```{r map-basics}
new_zealand <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(
  map_dir,
  "countries-nz-nz-all.geo.json"
))
hcmap(new_zealand, showInLegend = FALSE) |>
  hc_title(text = "New Zealand") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
```

## Income around the world

This is the international income example from the earlier homepage. The
`treemap` package supplies 2014 gross national income per capita. Join its
three-letter country code to the map's `iso-a3` property. A logarithmic color
scale makes the differences visible across the full range of incomes.

```{r world-income}
world <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(
  map_dir,
  "custom-world-robinson-lowres.geo.json"
))
data(GNI2014, package = "treemap")
head(GNI2014)

income_map <- hcmap(
  world,
  data = GNI2014,
  value = "GNI",
  joinBy = c("iso-a3", "iso3"),
  name = "GNI per capita",
  borderWidth = 0.2,
  nullColor = "#eceef2"
) |>
  hc_title(text = "Gross national income per capita, 2014") |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    type = "logarithmic",
    stops = color_stops(
      colors = c(
        "#000004",
        "#56106E",
        "#BB3754",
        "#F98C0A",
        "#FCFFA4"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(valuePrefix = "$", valueDecimals = 0) |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
income_map
```

## Map properties and joins

The join keys depend on the selected map. `get_data_from_map()` exposes those
properties. The package's local world boundaries use `iso3`; map-collection
boundaries commonly use `iso-a2`, `iso-a3` or `hc-key`.

```{r map-properties}
get_data_from_map(worldgeojson) |>
  select(any_of(c("name", "iso3", "continent"))) |>
  head()
```

To save boundaries for offline use, call `download_map_data()` once and retain
the returned object with your project. Pass it as `mapData` to a map series.

```{r offline-map, eval=FALSE}
boundaries <- download_map_data("custom/world-robinson-lowres")
saveRDS(boundaries, "world-map.rds")
```

## European time zones

Categorical maps use named data classes rather than a continuous scale.
These are standard-time groups, without seasonal daylight-saving adjustments.

```{r europe-zones}
zones <- data.frame(
  country = c(
    "PT",
    "IE",
    "GB",
    "IS",
    "FR",
    "DE",
    "ES",
    "IT",
    "NO",
    "SE",
    "PL",
    "AT",
    "CH",
    "FI",
    "EE",
    "LV",
    "LT",
    "GR",
    "RO",
    "BG"
  ),
  value = c(rep(0, 4), rep(1, 9), rep(2, 7))
)
europe <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(map_dir, "custom-europe.geo.json"))
hcmap(
  europe,
  data = zones,
  value = "value",
  joinBy = c("iso-a2", "country"),
  name = "Standard time",
  dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{point.country}")
) |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    dataClassColor = "category",
    dataClasses = list(
      list(from = 0, to = 0, name = "UTC"),
      list(from = 1, to = 1, name = "UTC + 1"),
      list(from = 2, to = 2, name = "UTC + 2")
    )
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Standard time in Europe")
```

## Points and bubbles

Longitude and latitude place points on the basemap. Add a magnitude with `z`
to turn those locations into bubbles. These are selected international airports
in South America; the values below are illustrative connection counts.

```{r airports}
airports <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "Santiago",
    "Buenos Aires",
    "São Paulo",
    "Lima",
    "Bogotá",
    "Quito",
    "Montevideo",
    "Asunción",
    "La Paz"
  ),
  lat = c(-33.39, -34.82, -23.44, -12.02, 4.70, -0.13, -34.84, -25.24, -16.51),
  lon = c(
    -70.79,
    -58.54,
    -46.47,
    -77.11,
    -74.15,
    -78.36,
    -56.03,
    -57.52,
    -68.19
  ),
  z = c(35, 40, 65, 42, 50, 24, 16, 14, 12)
)
boundaries <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(
  map_dir,
  "custom-south-america.geo.json"
))
south_america <- hcmap(boundaries, showInLegend = FALSE)
south_america |>
  hc_add_series(
    airports,
    type = "mappoint",
    name = "Airports",
    hcaes(lon = lon, lat = lat, name = name)
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Airports in South America")

south_america |>
  hc_add_series(
    airports,
    type = "mapbubble",
    name = "Illustrative connections",
    hcaes(lon = lon, lat = lat, z = z, name = name),
    maxSize = "12%"
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Locations with a magnitude")
```

## Projection and initial view

Set a projection, center and zoom through `hc_mapView()`. Coordinates are always
longitude first and latitude second.

```{r map-view}
globe <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(map_dir, "custom-world.geo.json"))
hcmap(globe, showInLegend = FALSE) |>
  hc_mapView(
    projection = list(name = "Orthographic"),
    center = c(-65, -20),
    zoom = 1
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "A view centered on South America") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
```

## Web tiles and other geographic series

`mapline` draws boundaries, `geoheatmap` colors geographic cells and `flowmap`
connects places. A tiled map requests tiles as readers move around.

```{r web-tiles, eval=FALSE}
highchart(type = "map") |>
  hc_mapView(center = c(-70.67, -33.45), zoom = 9) |>
  hc_add_series(type = "tiledwebmap", provider = list(type = "OpenStreetMap"))
```

[Highcharts Maps documentation](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/maps/getting-started)
